_comment: Tier-2 for dune::nonlinear#0, #1, #2 and dune::navier_stokes#0, #1 — one nonlinear problem, -div((1+u^2) grad u) = 1 on an 8x8 grid, supports all five, and grouping them keeps it to the forms already in the cache (wall time 2 s, 2026-08-06, dune-fem 2.12.0.2). Measured: a form written in the discrete solution carries ONE argument and galerkin() rejects it with ValueError 'Integrands model requires form with at least two arguments.'; both working spellings converge to the same answer (max 0.07446243 either way, a == b and F == 0); solve() returns a plain dict with keys ['converged', 'iterations', 'linear_iterations', 'timing'], here 2 Newton and 19 linear iterations, and its repr does NOT contain the retracted 'Newton did not converge' string. PRECISION NOTE on navier_stokes#0: dot(b, grad(u))*v is only illegal when the velocity is VECTOR-valued. With a SCALAR u the same expression builds fine — measured — because dot(b, grad(u)) is then a scalar. On a dimRange=2 space it raises ValueError 'Invalid ranks 1 and 1 in product.' as claimed, and inner(dot(grad(u), u), v)*dx is the spelling that works. The fixture checks both so the claim cannot be re-read as applying to scalar problems.
expect_in_output: Integrands model requires form with at least two arguments.
